sentences.text: This ancient fish featured a row of spines rising from its back fins, a characteristic shared with other members of its group.
Its mouth contained multi-cusped teeth with sharp accessory tines designed to impale prey for swallowing whole.
Individuals could reach lengths of up to 3.5 meters.
The genus was named by Soler-Gijon in 1997.
The type species of the genus is Lebachacanthus senckenbergianus.
This species was previously known as Orthacanthus senckenbergianus, described by Fritsch in 1889.
Well-preserved specimens originally identified as Orthacanthus were found in the Meisenheim Formation in Germany.
As apex predators in late Paleozoic freshwater ecosystems, these xenacanths hunted small amphibians.
They patrolled both freshwater and marine waters, possibly preying on temnospondyl and acanthodian larvae.
The species exhibited sexual dimorphism, with females possessing longer fin spines than males.
Lebachacanthus is a member of the class Chondrichthyes.
It belongs to the parent group Diplodoselachidae.
The animal is classified in the family Diplodoselachidae.
Lebachacanthus lived in Europe during the late Carboniferous and Early Permian periods.
